FailureKind.description:
What a failure is, so the app can offer the matching fix. `encoder`
(slim): the encoder the receiver requested could not start or failed;
the receiver is told, and another encoding chosen in its portal may work.
`receiver` (slim): the receiver is unavailable (not lighting, unreachable,
or its name does not resolve); the worker keeps reconnecting. `version`
(slim): Prysm speaks another capture stream version; both need the same
release, and the worker retries every 10 s. `other`: anything else.

Flavor.description: Which package this supervisor belongs to.

subscribe.description: Keep sending the state on every change.

LightingTarget.description: What the user wants the LEDs to do.

oneOf.description: Waiting before the next start after a failure.

seconds.description:
Whole seconds until the next start, rounded up, when this state
was sent (at least 1). The app counts down from when it received
it; no clock is shared.

Preferences.description:
`tv.json` and the `setPreferences` request (complete, every field
optional). Fields marked "Slim only" must stay unset (`null` or absent)
in the full package.

autostart.description: Start enabled (full: processed lighting) when the service starts.

instance.description:
Slim only: the headless Prysm's address, such as
`http://192.168.1.20:8787` or `https://prysm.example.com` (through a
reverse proxy). The TV streams its picture there, and the TV app
links to its portal. Only the syntax is checked when saved; the TV
resolves a host name at every connection attempt, and one that does
not resolve is reported as the receiver wait.

enabled.description: Slim: frames should flow. Full: processed lighting (or off).

SlimEncoding.description:
How the slim package encodes the frames it sends: the encoding its
receiver requested (set in the desktop portal). Exactly this encoder is
used; one that cannot start or fails is a failure, never a switch to
another. `h264_hardware`: the TV's hardware H.264 encoder (about
2 Mbit/s); `h264_software`: OpenH264 on the TV's CPU (about 2 Mbit/s);
`raw`: uncompressed NV12 (320x180 at 30 fps is about 21 Mbit/s).

State.description:
The `getState` reply and subscription payload (plus LS2's `returnValue`).
Fields marked "Full only" are `null` in the slim package.

capturing.description:
Frames are flowing. Full: lighting runs and frames arrive (false
while it waits for video). Slim: frames were sent in the last second.
Always false unless `worker` is `running`.

enabled.description: Slim: frames should flow. Full: lighting is not off.

oneOf.description:
Slim only: the encoding of the frames being sent while connected to
the receiver; always the one the receiver requested (set in the
desktop portal's remote capture settings).

The current failure (or, slim, the receiver wait): what it is and
its message with the causes.

flavor.description: The installed package; both install as `io.prysm.tv`.

fps.description:
Frames per second over about the last second, rounded, while the
worker measures them (full: lighting runs; slim: connected and
sending); 0 while it waits for frames. Always null unless `worker` is
`running`.

oneOf.description: Full only: the engine's target, including changes made in the portal.

log.description: The latest worker stderr lines, oldest first (at most 20).

paused.description:
Slim only: the receiver paused the stream because its lighting is
off; the TV capture is stopped until the receiver asks again. Not a
failure. Always false unless `worker` is `running`.

portal.description: Full only: the portal's LAN address once the worker reported it.

subscribed.description: On `getState` and subscription updates: whether the caller is subscribed.

StateReply.description: A successful state reply: [`State`] with LS2's `returnValue`.

WorkerFailure.description: A failure: what it is and its message with the causes.

message.description: What failed, with its cause chain (cut to 1 KiB).
